rationale: A source-explained negative result that grounds the counterevidence of the empty-Entries read-index finding: the response direction of the same message family is validated, while the request direction is not. Source trace: stepFollower's MsgReadIndexResp case rejects any entry count other than one with an error log and only then appends the read state (raft.go:1766-1771), whereas the request direction reaches Entries[0] unchecked (raft.go:1346-1363, 2142-2157, read_only.go:56-63). The experiment feeds zero-entry, two-entry and one-entry responses into a real follower and reports whether each was accepted, with the same recovery wrapper used elsewhere so that a panic would be visible rather than crashing the harness.

investigations.question: Does the read-index response path validate the shape of a peer-delivered MsgReadIndexResp before accepting it as a local read state, and how does that compare with the request path that dereferences Entries[0] unchecked?
investigations.hypothesis: stepFollower accepts a MsgReadIndexResp only when it carries exactly one entry and otherwise logs an error and returns without touching the read states, so malformed responses are rejected at the follower, while the request direction on the leader has no corresponding entry-count check.
investigations.discriminator: Step MsgReadIndexResp messages with zero, two and one entries into a real follower of a three-voter cluster and record for each whether the node panicked, how many read states were added, the index and request context of any added state, and the node state. The one-entry case is the control that must be accepted; the zero and two-entry cases must be rejected without a panic and without adding a read state. If a malformed response is accepted or aborts the node, the hypothesis is refuted.
limitations: The responses are stepped directly into the follower; the transport and the Node layer's own filtering of response messages from unknown peers are not exercised.
Only the follower's response handling is probed; the leader-side request handling is covered by the earlier questions.
The probe covers the shape validation only, not whether an accepted response corresponds to a request the node actually issued.

knowledge.statement: stepFollower handles MsgReadIndexResp by requiring exactly one entry: with any other count it logs an error naming the sender and the count and returns without recording anything, and only for a single-entry message does it append a ReadState carrying the message index and the entry data as the request context (raft.go:1766-1771). The read-index request direction has no comparable check: the leader's producer reaches Entries[0] through sendMsgReadIndexResponse and readOnly.addRequest (raft.go:1346-1363, 2142-2157, read_only.go:56-63).
knowledge.conditions: The receiver is a follower in the same term as the response's sender and reaches stepFollower's MsgReadIndexResp case; the message is delivered to the raft state machine directly.

scope.description: Three probes on one freshly elected three-voter cluster: MsgReadIndexResp messages carrying zero, two and one entries are stepped into follower 2 at its own term, each with the panic recovered and the resulting read states recorded.
assumptions: The cluster is built with newTestRaft for {1,2,3} and elected with nt.send(MsgHup), so follower 2 is in the leader's term and knows its leader.
Each response is delivered as pb.Message{From: 1, To: 2, Type: MsgReadIndexResp, Term: follower term, Index: 7, Entries: ...}, which is the shape the leader's response producer emits.
Panics are recovered by the harness only; the recovered value is reported verbatim.
A read state is considered accepted when the follower's readStates slice grows, and its index and request context are reported.
excluded: The transport and the Node layer's response filtering
Any correlation between an accepted response and a request the node issued
Snapshots, membership changes, restarts and leadership changes

experiment.prefix: Harness (draft file assurance_generated_test.go, package raft, execution package '.'; no captured file is replaced). The test builds three real raft instances with newTestRaft(1|2|3, 10, 1, newTestMemoryStorage(withPeers(1,2,3))) and elects node 1 with newNetwork and nt.send(MsgHup); it asserts that node 1 is StateLeader and clears all queues. For each probe it emits read_index_resp_setup with probe_id, scenario, node, node state, term, lead, the number of entries to be sent and the read index (7), then steps the message into follower 2 inside a recover wrapper and records whether the node panicked and with which text. Afterwards it processes the follower's own queues, computes how many read states were added relative to the count before the step, reads the index and request context of the newest read state, and emits read_index_resp_outcome with probe_id, scenario, entries_sent, panicked, recovered, read_states_added, read_state_index, read_state_request_ctx, node state and term. Probes: 'resp/zero-entries' (no entries), 'resp/two-entries' (two entries) and 'resp/one-entry' (one entry, the control). The test asserts that the accepted response carried a non-nil request context, so a silently empty acceptance cannot be mistaken for validation.
experiment.responsibility: The read-index response path owns rejecting a peer-delivered message whose shape cannot be interpreted as a read state for the local node, so that a malformed response neither produces a bogus read state nor aborts the node.

comparisons.description: A MsgReadIndexResp with no entries adds no read state and does not abort the follower.
A MsgReadIndexResp with two entries adds no read state and does not abort the follower.
Control: a MsgReadIndexResp with exactly one entry is accepted as one read state carrying the request context.
